correctness.rationale: For both eleven-point graph6 complement encodings I decoded the exact flag one-skeleta and independently enumerated every one of the 30 edges, all triangular faces and every graph automorphism, rather than trusting VERIFY_OK. Each has f=(11,30,20), cyclic vertex links and no four-clique, so is a combinatorial closed surface; Euler characteristic 1 plus the cited RP2 characterization establishes the intended type. For an edge ab with opposite vertices c,d, deleting ab and adding cd preserves the flag 2-complex exactly when N(c)∩N(d)={a,b}: otherwise an extra triangle appears, while with precisely a,b the changed cliques are exactly the two replacement triangles and no four-clique exists. Independent graph enumeration gave exactly five legal labeled flips for graph6 JCpdUg{[ap_ and four for JCp`eikYa|?, with the stated removed/added edge lists. Each changed graph is isomorphic to the other and not itself; automorphism group orders are 10 and 8 and act transitively on the respective 5/4 edges. The global two-type assertion follows from Van Tuyl Theorem 1.1 for connected complement graphs, together with the elementary no-nontrivial-join fact for closed RP2 triangulations (a join triangulated closed surface is a sphere); it does not assert a fresh independent 1,006,700,565-graph census.
